title: AI Process Audit intake
description: A structured description of a business and the processes it runs. This is the only input to the engine. Every field asks for something a business owner can answer from memory, which is why there are no cost fields, no case identifiers, and no org chart.

schema_version.description: Version of this intake schema the file was written against. 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 each add one optional field and remove nothing, so a document written against 1.2.0 still satisfies this schema and is still accepted. Earlier versions are not, because 1.2.0 removed an enum value and 1.1.0 made a field required. See docs/roadmap.md on tightening this before anything starts generating intake files.

intake_id.description: Optional stable identifier for this intake, used to match gold labels in the eval harness.

collected_on.description: Date the intake was collected, as YYYY-MM-DD.

name.description: Trading name of the business. Optional so intakes can be anonymised.

industry.description: What the business does, in the words the business would use.

headcount.description: Total number of people, including part time and owners.

tools_in_use.description: Software the business already pays for or relies on, across the whole business.

notes.description: Anything about the business that does not fit the fields above.

id.description: Stable identifier for this process. Required in practice for gold labelling. Generated from the name if absent.

name.description: Short name for the process as staff would refer to it.

description.description: How the process runs today, start to finish, in order. Step inference reads this field, so ordering words such as then, next, and once are useful.

volume.description: How many items the process handles, and over what period.

count.description: Number of items. An estimate is fine and is expected.

unit.description: What is being counted, for example invoices, bookings, applications.

period.description: The period the count covers. Use per_run when the count is items handled each time the process runs.

is_estimate.description: True when the business guessed the number rather than reading it from a system.

roles.description: Job titles of the people involved. Used to attribute steps in the process map.

hours_per_run.description: Total person hours consumed each time the process runs, across everyone involved.

current_tools.description: Software and non software tools used in this specific process. Paper, phone, and whiteboard are valid entries.

pain_description.description: What goes wrong, what it costs, and who feels it. Scored directly by the pain criterion.

time_spent.description: How much time this process takes. This is the denominator behind the return band criterion, so it is required. Give whichever of the two is easier to answer, or both. An estimate is expected.

hours_per_week.description: Total hours a week the process consumes across everyone involved.

minutes_per_case.description: Minutes spent on one item, end to end, across everyone who touches it. Combined with volume to work out the yearly figure.

decision_type.description: Optional. What kind of thinking the process requires. rule_based means the same inputs always give the same answer and the rules could be written down. judgment_heavy means an experienced person weighs things up and two of them might disagree. mixed means both, usually a rule based path with exceptions. Read by the implementation risk criterion. Absent means not reported, which is scored conservatively rather than assumed to be simple.

baseline_metric.description: Optional. Any number the business already tracks for this process today, in their own words, for example 'invoices out within 3 days, currently about 40 percent'. Null or absent means nothing is tracked, which caps the return band because there would be no way to show the automation helped.

customer_facing.description: Optional. True when a mistake in this process is seen by a customer rather than caught inside the business. Read by the implementation risk criterion as the size of the blast radius.

exception_rate.description: Optional. Roughly how many cases out of ten need handling differently from the normal path. rare is about one in ten or fewer, occasional is around two or three in ten, frequent is four or more in ten. Answer from memory, not from a system. Read by the implementation risk criterion, because a long tail of exceptions is what breaks an automation after launch rather than during the build. Absent means not reported and is read conservatively as occasional.

planned_system_change.description: Optional. A system change the business already intends to make that touches this process, for example replacing the tool it runs in. Absent means not reported. This field feeds none of the six scoring criteria and changes no score, cap, or band. It appears in the report as a sequencing note, because a process about to move to a different system is a question of when and how to automate rather than whether.

description.description: What is changing, in the words the business would use.

timeframe.description: Optional. Roughly when. Absent means the business did not say.

risk_flags.description: Optional. Properties of the process that raise implementation risk. Absent means none were reported, not that none exist. Whether a process is customer facing is not listed here, because it has its own field.

data_notes.description: Optional. Where the information lives and what shape it is in. Read by the data availability criterion.

owner.description: Optional. The person accountable for the process.
